sample_unit: single application case; 78 scoring test cases, 52 usability participants (14 clinicians, 26 patients, 12 older adults), 926 author messages, 23 storage canaries

links.outcome: Errors found by independent clinical review versus passing automated tests of scoring matrix
links.effect: All 78 original automated cases passed, but independent review found 17 expected results requiring clinical or methodological correction.
links.quote: Although all 78 original automated cases passed, independent review found 17 expected results requiring clinical or methodological correction.

links.outcome: Measured accessibility parameters (text size, contrast) against WCAG 2.1
links.effect: Accessibility measurement found 10-px text and 2.56:1 contrast, despite mean SUS around 92.
links.quote: Accessibility measurement found 10-px text and 2.56:1 contrast.

links.outcome: Undocumented third-party data flow found by code audit versus privacy claim
links.effect: A third-party analytics tag contradicted the app's local-only privacy claim.
links.quote: Technical findings included instrument mislabelling, a manifest that failed installability validation, and a third-party analytics tag contradicting the local-only privacy claim.

unlisted_practices: Independent post-hoc code audit of clinician-built AI-assisted software
Requirements traceability analysis of AI-assisted development conversations
Persistent-storage (browser eviction) testing for offline web apps
Unaided home-screen installation testing in older adults

screen.reason: This empirical case study evaluates specific assurance, audit, and verification practices to catch defects in deployed clinician-built, AI-assisted health software.

primary.practice: multi-domain verification and independent clinical/technical assurance of AI-generated clinical software
